title: Grateful Dead Live at Music Hall on 1973-12-01
lineage: Maxell UD90's > Nakamichi CR-5A > Edirol FA-66 > Wavelab > R8Brain > CD-Wave > TLH > FLAC 1644 tagged. Transfer by Andrew F.
source: 2 source matrix by dusborne Soundboard (shnid:112205) SBD -> Master Reel -> Dat (44.1k); Transfer Info: Dat (Sony R500) -> Tascam SS-R05 -> Adobe Audition v3.0 -> Samplitude Professional 11.2 -> FLAC and Audience (shnid:110781) FOB AUD Source: Unknown equipment > MAC taped by Bill Degen. This transfer is 1st Gen cassettes, kindly provided by Tim Friend.

ai_review.summary: Brilliant Dusborne matrix capture of the December 1973 show, spotlighting a soaring Playing in the Band and a deep Uncle John’s Band jam.
ai_review.review: The recording is praised as the best among numerous existing tapes, with Dusborne's MTX blend delivering clear instrument separation and a well‑balanced mix. The performance shines especially on Playing in the Band (including its reprise) and the expansive Uncle John’s Band segment, while a few moments such as Row Jimmy sound slightly thin. Overall the show is regarded as one of the standout shows of ’73.

ai_rating.rationale: Consistently high praise for both the musical performance and the matrix recording quality across four reviews; only minor audio quibbles noted.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Dusborne's MTX blend is described as brilliant and well‑done, offering clear sound with excellent balance. One reviewer notes a slight thinning of the mix during Row Jimmy, but no major flaws are reported.

show_quality.setlist_flow: The second set launches with a powerful Dark Star/Other One vehicle, moves through an expansive Uncle John’s Band jam, and builds to a fiery Playing in the Band reprise, maintaining strong momentum throughout.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Garcia delivers crisp riffs and leads the jams, especially evident during Playing in the Band.
band_member_comments.Bob: Bob Weir commands the vocal coda on the Playin' reprise, showcasing his strong presence.
band_member_comments.Keys: Keith Godchaux provides supportive piano that reinforces Garcia’s motifs throughout the set.
